chapter_seo_title: Dao Gui Yi Xian Chapter 469 – Li Huowang Disperses His Legacy
chapter_meta_description: Li Huowang prepares Niuxin Village for his absence, distributing artifacts and alchemy. A quiet chapter of trust, mortality, and a reality-bending ending.
og_title: Li Huowang Hands Out His Last Lifelines
og_description: In a rare quiet moment, Li Huowang faces his own mortality and begins to build a Niuxin Village that can survive without him.
twitter_title: A General Before the Final March
twitter_description: Li Huowang gifts a phylactery, transfers secrets, and erases a worry from existence—all while everyone silently asks: is he coming back?

lore_anchors.definition: A palm-sized doll made from the cultivator’s own skin and mercury; functions as a phylactery allowing survival past decapitation, and can be mass-produced given enough time.

A bonded laborer in historical Chinese society, tied to a household or land. Not equivalent to chattel slavery; servants had some legal protections and could gain freedom. The term reflects rigid class hierarchy without implying total dehumanization.
A talisman-scepter symbolizing “as you wish,” corrupted here into a Heart-Element-tongue artifact that fills a target’s mind with bewilderment.
A basic alchemical pill for nourishing blood; taught in Qingfeng Temple, now transcribed for the village’s medical use.
An alchemical pill for fortifying the body’s foundation; included in the manual Li Huowang transcribes for Niuxin Village.
A government-sponsored supernormal law enforcement body believed to be under the imperial board of war; they hunt rogue cultivators and manage supernatural disasters.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why is Li Huowang giving away his most valuable items?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He’s preparing for his own possible death or insanity. After surviving so much, he’s forcing himself to build a Niuxin Village that can survive without him—a leader’s last duty.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What happened to Li Sui’s body in this chapter?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Li Sui now inhabits Mantou’s corpse, but the body is structurally weak—tentacles hold broken bones together, and organs are partly exposed. Li Huowang finds her both horrifying and still his daughter.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What does “erasing the written trouble” mean at the end?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Li Huowang uses his Heart-Element power to literally delete a line of text describing his worry about Heavenly Calamities. It’s a reality-bending ability that erases the *concept* of the problem, not just the words.
